text:
I need to tell our staff that we're ending fully remote work. I'm one of the three partners at an architecture firm with 46 architects and designers.

What I can say:
- From September 1, everyone works in the office on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.
- 15 of our people were hired as fully remote in 2021 and 2022. 4 of them live more than two hours from the office.
- Those 4 can keep working remotely until the end of next year. After that, they come in once a week.
- Last year we lost two large hospital projects in the final interview. Both clients told us our team seemed not to know each other.
- Based on our review records, junior staff hired since 2022 are taking about 30% longer to reach the point where they lead a project.
- The partners have been coming in one day a week. We'll be in all three days too.

Keep it to one page. It goes out by email before an all-staff meeting on Friday.

Before I draft this, five questions. Your answers will change what the email says:

1. **Which September, and which year-end?** Today is 16 November 2026. If the change starts 1 September 2027, then "end of next year" gives the four long-distance people only four months beyond everyone else. Is that what you mean, or do they keep remote work until the end of 2028?

2. **What about the other 11 people hired as fully remote?** They live within two hours, but they took the job on remote terms and may have arranged their lives around that. Are you offering them anything, such as help with travel costs, a later start date or a conversation one-to-one? If someone can't make it work, what happens? Can they ask for an exception or leave on agreed terms? If the email says nothing, people will assume the worst.

3. **Is there an exceptions process?** I mean for things like caring responsibilities, health or disability. If so, who do people talk to?

4. **What's decided and what's still open on Friday?** I assume the three days are fixed. Is anything up for discussion, like which three days or how Mondays and Fridays work?

5. **Who is it from?** Should it come from all three partners together or from you? Please give the names as they should appear in the sign-off.

If you don't know some of these yet, say so. I'll write around those gaps rather than guess.

1. End of next year means end of 2027. That's what I can commit to for those four.

2. We'll pay up to $150 a month toward commuting for anyone who lives more than 30 miles away. I can't offer exceptions to anyone beyond those 4. I don't know what happens if someone can't make it work.

3. No. I can't offer exceptions beyond those 4. People can bring questions to me or to HR before Friday.

4. The three days are fixed. We'll review the policy with staff after six months. I don't know about Mondays and Fridays.

5. From me, Paul Whitaker.

<final_document>
Subject: Three office days a week from September 1, 2027

Everyone,

From September 1, 2027, everyone at the firm will work in the office on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays. That includes the three partners. This email explains why we're making the change, what it means for those of you it affects most, and what help we're offering. We'll talk it through together at Friday's all-staff meeting.

**Why we're doing this**

Last year we reached the final interview for two large hospital projects and lost both. Both clients gave us the same reason: our team seemed not to know each other. A client hiring for a hospital is choosing a team to work with for years, and they could tell we didn't yet work as one.

We're seeing the same thing inside the firm. Our review records show that junior staff hired since 2022 are taking about 30% longer to reach the point of leading a project. That isn't their fault. People learn to lead projects by working next to people who already do it: hearing how a client call is handled, getting pulled into a markup, asking a quick question instead of saving it for a meeting. Working remotely has meant much less of that.

**The partners too**

For the past few years the partners have come in one day a week. That's been part of the problem, so we're changing it. We'll be in all three days, the same as everyone else.

**If you were hired as fully remote**

Fifteen of you joined in 2021 and 2022 as fully remote. You took the job on those terms, and this changes them. I know that's a real cost to some of you, and I won't pretend it isn't.

Four of you live more than two hours from the office. You can keep working remotely until the end of 2027. From January 2028, we'll ask you to come in one day a week.

Apart from those four, we aren't able to make individual exceptions. I would rather tell you that plainly now than leave you guessing.

**Help with commuting**

From September 1, we'll pay up to $150 a month toward commuting costs for anyone who lives more than 30 miles from the office.

**What's fixed and what's open**

The three days are fixed. Six months after we start, we'll review with you how the policy is working.

If you have questions or concerns, please come to me or to HR before Friday. If this is going to be hard for you, I would rather hear it now.

Paul Whitaker
</final_document>

A few things to be ready for:

- **Which year:** Since it's already November 2026, I've assumed the start date is September 1, 2027. Change it if that's wrong.
- **Questions on Friday:** The two you're most likely to get are the ones you couldn't answer yet: what happens if someone can't make this work, and whether Mondays and Fridays are flexible. The email doesn't mention either. It would help to have at least a holding answer for both before the meeting.
- **The no-exceptions line:** I stated it outright because you told me there are none. Leaving it out would let people hope for something you can't give. It will still be the hardest sentence for people to read.
